_description: MFJ filer with spouse aging past 65 mid-simulation. Locks in the fix for the spouse-age propagation bug: the senior add-on (and OBBB bonus) must qualify the spouse based on their year-adjusted age, not the reference-year value.
_rationale: Self age 67 (already 65+, qualifies every year), spouse age 63 (under 65 at start). $50k/yr pension. 2026 MFJ std deduction $32,200, MFJ per-senior add-on $1,650, OBBB $6,000/qualifying-senior (no phaseout since gross < $150k MFJ threshold). Years 0–1: only self qualifies (1 senior) → ded $32,200 + $1,650 + $6,000 = $39,850 → taxable $10,150 → fed tax 10% × $10,150 = $1,015. Years 2+ (spouse age 65+): both qualify (2 seniors) → ded $32,200 + $3,300 + $12,000 = $47,500 → taxable $2,500 → fed tax 10% × $2,500 = $250. Pre-fix bug would freeze spouse at 63 forever → years 2-4 would also show $1,015. FL state (0% rate). No state tax, no LTCG, no NIIT, no IRMAA. No growth, no inflation → tax assertions are exact.
name: Spouse Senior Add-On Aging
